hooks.text: A massive asteroid once reached the highest hazard rating in history.
Which asteroid was once given a 1-in-37 chance of hitting Earth?
The world's most dangerous asteroid is not actually going to hit us.

title: The Asteroid Passing Closer Than Our Satellites
description: Apophis was once considered the most dangerous rock in the sky. In 2029, it returns for a record-breaking flyby closer than our own satellites.

beats.text: A massive asteroid once reached the highest hazard rating in history.
beats.visual: artist's concept of asteroid Apophis approaching a glowing Earth, NASA, 2020

beats.text: In 2004, astronomers calculated that asteroid Apophis had a 2.7 percent chance of hitting Earth.
beats.visual: photograph of the Kitt Peak National Observatory telescope domes at dusk, 2004

beats.text: It was the first object to ever hit Level 4 on the Torino scale.
beats.visual: diagram of the Torino Impact Hazard Scale chart, NASA, 2005

beats.text: Radar data from 2021 eventually ruled out an impact for at least a century.
beats.visual: photograph of the Goldstone Deep Space Communications Complex 70-meter antenna, 2021

beats.text: But on Friday, April 13, 2029, the 450-meter rock will still sweep incredibly close.
beats.visual: radar delay Doppler imagery of asteroid Apophis, Goldstone Observatory, 2021

beats.text: Apophis will pass within 31,600 kilometers, flying lower than many of our own satellites.
beats.visual: diagram of Apophis path relative to geostationary satellite orbit, ESA, 2024

beats.text: Billions of people across Europe and Africa can watch it with the naked eye.
beats.visual: artist concept of asteroid Apophis as a bright star in the night sky, 2029

beats.text: Earth’s gravity will even stretch the asteroid’s surface and trigger minor landslides.
beats.visual: artist's concept of tidal forces affecting the surface of asteroid Apophis, ESA, 2024

beats.text: This intense cosmic encounter will forever alter the orbit of this massive asteroid.
beats.visual: diagram showing asteroid orbit changing from Aten to Apollo class, NASA, 2024
